info.name: OIPPP API - Test Plan section 13
info.description: API-level runs of the Test Plan test cases. Run the folders in order (newman runs the whole collection): they share tokens and ids, and the three waits keep each block inside the 10-per-minute auth limit (SEC-5).

item.name: 00 Setup
item.description: Admin login and two approved recruiters (R1 owns the listings, R2 does not).

item.name: R1 posts LST-4 listing closing in 30 s
TC-AUTH-01
item.description: AUTH-1, AUTH-2: register a student, reject a duplicate email.

exec: pm.test('role STUDENT, status ACTIVE', () => { pm.expect(user.role).to.eql('STUDENT'); pm.expect(user.status).to.eql('ACTIVE'); });
pm.test('duplicate message', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.eql('An account with this email already exists'));

item.name: TC-SRCH-01
item.description: SRCH-1, SRCH-2, SRCH-3 on a run-unique keyword. The 5,000-listing version is in tests/integration/listing-search-performance.test.js.

exec: pm.test('exactly the two REMOTE listings with stipend >= 10000', () => pm.expect(pagination.total).to.eql(2));
pm.test('every result OPEN, REMOTE, stipend >= 10000', () => listings.forEach((l) => {
pm.test('sorted by deadline', () => listings.forEach((l, i) => i && pm.expect(new Date(l.deadline) >= new Date(listings[i - 1].deadline)).to.be.true));
pm.test('pages of 20 with a total', () => { pm.expect(pagination.limit).to.eql(20); pm.expect(pagination.total).to.be.a('number'); });
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ company: 'Globex', title: 'Plain Role ' + pm.environment.get('run'),
location: 'Pune', mode: 'REMOTE', stipend: 9000, skills: ['Kotlin'], deadline: pm.environment.get('tomorrow') }) } });

exec: pm.variables.set('qBody', JSON.stringify({ text: 'Question ' + (n + 1) + ' ' + pm.environment.get('run'), topic: topics[n % 4],
pm.variables.set('tBody', JSON.stringify({ title: 'T1 ' + pm.environment.get('run'), durationMin: 30, questionIds: JSON.parse(pm.environment.get('qIds')) }));

exec: pm.test('timer counts from the original start', () => pm.expect(a.endsAt).to.eql(pm.environment.get('endsAt')));
